clue.text: Record roles played around university? A revelation

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: the rearranged roles goes round the next piece, holding it inside
the word roles is performed in a new form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor's recorded roles, made around a university, turn out to be quite an eye-opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' reads as a verb but is a noun here; 'played' scrambles the roles (LOSRE) and 'around' wraps them round the university letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something disclosed is a thing made known, a revelation.

clue.text: Attractive young woman producing laughter when ignoring rule

indicators.note: ignoring tells us to leave the following letter out of the word before

parts.note: something droll is amusing, causing laughter

explanation.surface: A pretty girl who makes people laugh, provided she forgets the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal sense: a doll is slang for a pretty young woman.

clue.text: Castle in southern Switzerland facing damage

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)
loss can mean harm or damage suffered

explanation.surface: A castle in the south of Switzerland is suffering damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Loan word: a schloss is the German word for a castle or manor house.

clue.text: Detail even I'd confused after opening to long film

indicators.note: after places the rearranged words behind the single letter
the opening of a word is its first letter, taken here from long
the words detail even I'd are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a long film's detail has confused even them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges DETAILEVENID into IVEANDLETDIE, which comes 'after' L, the opening letter of 'long'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the 1973 James Bond movie with Roger Moore bears this title.

clue.text: Boil first of eggs in group associated with nameless bird

indicators.note: in places the egg letter inside the word for group

parts.note: a set is a group of things

indicators.note: the first letter of eggs is picked
nameless means losing the abbreviation for name from the bird

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Boiling eggs alongside a bird with no name, as a cooking instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' drops N (name) from HEN to leave HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to seethe is to bubble as if boiling, now usually of anger.

clue.text: Cut back sides of rare fish round river

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters, here of rare
the fish goes round the river letter

parts.note: a tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A rare fish found swimming round a river is being cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to retrench is to reduce spending, to cut back.

clue.text: Fix special academic stream

parts.note: the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge, a university town

explanation.surface: Arranging a special place on an academic course.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a fix is a rigged deal, a swindle or con.

clue.text: Coastal road bypassing hotel? It's seen at top of building

definitions.text: It's seen at top of building

indicators.note: bypassing means going round and missing out the hotel letter

parts.note: a corniche is a road cut along a coastal cliff
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A seaside road that skirts a hotel, with something visible on the roofline.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a cornice is the ornamental moulding running along the top of a building or wall.

clue.text: A visitor avoiding square in Mediterranean island for seeds

indicators.note: in puts the A and the trimmed visitor inside the island

parts.note: Malta is an island in the Mediterranean

indicators.note: avoiding means the square letter is left out of the visitor

parts.note: a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: A tourist on a Mediterranean island steering clear of the town square, looking for seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' drops S (square) from GUEST to leave GUET; with A that goes 'in' MALTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Specific term: malaguetta is the pungent seed also called grains of paradise, used as a spice.

clue.text: In general, hesitate having lost sight of English port

indicators.note: having lost sight of means one letter for English goes missing
In puts the hesitating word inside the general

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
to haver is to dither or hesitate

explanation.surface: A general dithers and loses track of an English port.
explanation.walkthrough: HAVER placed 'In' LEE gives LHAVEREE; 'having lost sight of' E drops one E to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the French city is a major seaport on the Seine estuary in Normandy.

clue.text: Acrobat switching directions to make cart

indicators.note: directions here are left and right, whose letters swap places

parts.note: a tumbler is an acrobat who does somersaults

explanation.surface: An acrobat changes direction and turns into a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching directions' swaps L (left) and R (right) in TUMBLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Specific term: a tumbrel was a farm cart, famous for carrying victims to the guillotine.

clue.text: Friend with nervous habit hoarding currency abroad is this?

definitions.text: Friend with nervous habit hoarding currency abroad is this?

indicators.note: hoarding means the pair holds the currency and is between them

parts.note: a mate is a friend
a tic is a nervous twitch or habit
the rial is the currency of Iran and other countries

explanation.surface: A twitchy pal who hoards foreign money must be someone obsessed with wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: someone hoarding cash cares mainly about money and possessions.

clue.text: Barely funded — how one might describe sole British singer round back of bar?

parts.note: a sole is found on a shoe, so its position is described with that phrase

indicators.note: the singer goes round the letter taken from bar

parts.note: Sting is the British rock singer, formerly of the Police

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, here of bar

explanation.surface: A lone British singer performing round the back of a bar, with hardly any money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like 'only', but it is the underside of footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: doing something with very little money is doing it cheaply, on minimal funds.

clue.text: A prison rep reformed underworld leader

indicators.note: the words a prison rep are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A prison representative turns over a new leaf as a gangland boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld leader' suggests a crime boss; it is the queen of Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythology: Proserpina is the Roman name for Persephone, queen of the underworld.

clue.text: Live fairground entertainment catching last of the sun

indicators.note: catching means the ride holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a ride is an attraction at a fair

indicators.note: the last letter of the is taken

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: A fairground ride enjoyed live while catching the last of the sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to reside somewhere is to live there, as a verb of dwelling.

clue.text: Director putting film music around timeless film locations

indicators.note: around places the music round the trimmed locations

parts.note: a score is the music written for a film

indicators.note: timeless removes the T for time from the word

parts.note: sets are where scenes are filmed

explanation.surface: A film director setting a soundtrack across his various locations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' takes T (time) out of SETS to leave SES.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Martin Scorsese is the American film director of Taxi Driver and Goodfellas.

clue.text: State aiming for change to embrace China

indicators.note: the rearranged word embraces, or holds, the abbreviation for China
aiming for change means the word aiming has its letters altered

parts.note: CH is an abbreviation for China

explanation.surface: A political statement about aiming for change by embracing China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for change' gives MIIGAN, and 'to embrace' has it wrap round the porcelain country's short form; 'State' sits at the front looking like a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the fifty US states, on the Great Lakes.

clue.text: Careless person getting recurrent fine in country

parts.note: a sloven is someone untidy and careless

indicators.note: recurrent, running back, has the word for fine read backwards

parts.note: A1 (written AI) means first-class or fine

explanation.surface: A sloppy individual keeps picking up fines in some foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning first-rate, is written with a letter I standing in for the digit; 'recurrent' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a central European country, formerly part of Yugoslavia, capital Ljubljana.

clue.text: Rolling work unionist provided

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
U is an abbreviation for Unionist in Northern Irish politics
lent means provided on loan

explanation.surface: A rolling work programme provided by a Unionist politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling' is not moving but 'rolling in it', very rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone rolling in money is wealthy, as lavish and luxurious riches suggest.

clue.text: Slam beef, latest in defective meat

parts.note: to beef is to complain, as does to carp

indicators.note: latest in means the last letters of defective and meat

explanation.surface: A food critic slams beef as the latest in a line of faulty meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' is the verb to grumble, not the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal sense: to carpet someone is to reprimand them severely, to criticise.

clue.text: Plant, favourite one bordering educational body

indicators.note: bordering puts the single letter at the edge of the educational body

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
uni is short for university
a means one

explanation.surface: A favourite plant grows at the edge of a college campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a garden flower with trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Film company boss with idol regularly

parts.note: a stud is a raised knob or boss

indicators.note: regularly takes alternate letters of idol

explanation.surface: A movie studio chief teams up with a star idol on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' suggests a chief, but here it is a decorative knob.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a studio is a film production company, as in the Hollywood majors.

clue.text: Demented hounds twitter nervously

indicators.note: the letters of hounds twitter jitter about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Mad dogs chatter and yelp in a nervous frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom: going round the bend or twist means becoming crazy.

clue.text: Neat pottery left out

indicators.note: out shows the abbreviation for left is removed

parts.note: Delft is blue and white glazed pottery from the Dutch town

explanation.surface: Tidy pottery that has been left out on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: deft and neat both mean skilful and dexterous.

clue.text: Titanic obstacle beginning to impede Anglican composer

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of impede

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: A church composer runs into an enormous obstacle at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titanic' is the ship that sank in 1912, not just 'huge'.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: the liner Titanic sank after hitting a floating mass of ice in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Leaders in dispute eager to eliminate needless tension engaged in this?

definitions.text: Leaders in dispute eager to eliminate needless tension engaged in this?

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of each of the following words

parts.words: dispute eager to eliminate needless tension engaged

explanation.surface: Heads of rival parties keen to defuse pointless hostility take part in peace talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an easing of hostility between nations is what such parties pursue.

clue.text: Wine enthusiastically imbibed

indicators.note: imbibed means drunk in, so the word is held within enthusiastically

explanation.surface: A wine drunk with great enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Italian sparkling white wine from Piedmont.

clue.text: Union I cast wrongly as unconcerned

indicators.note: the words union I cast are set out wrongly, in a different order

explanation.surface: A union member casts a vote wrongly but doesn't care.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone nonchalant shows no worry, carefree and casual.
